review_comments: Could this exception occur for other reasons than a corrupted file?
As far as i understand, OSError will also catch these related errors: BlockingIOError , PermissionError, TimeoutError

So there's a range of reasons this could be failing, but falling back to the backup file only makes sense if the current file is corrupted, so we should catch a more precise error. Maybe we can do a check on the error message contents.

For instance, if there's a permission issue, then it doesn't make sense to fall back to the other file (which also won't load). You just want to raise the first exception to the user.

I've dive deeper into hdf5 backend and ... there are thouthands of errors related to file reading: https://github.com/search?q=repo%3AHDFGroup%2Fhdf5+HGOTO_ERROR&type=code

It seems not possible to catch only subset of them. Even in my test case error message is "Unable to open file (file signature not found)"  which is far from original issue "Unable to synchronously open file (bad object header version number)"

I suppose we should ether leave OSError capturing or try to load previous weights without copying
